transcript.text: Samsung microwave runs, light on, plate turns, fan going, but the food comes out stone cold. Watched a YouTube video on testing the magnetron - I've got the cover screws out already, what should I check first?

I can't guide any testing or work inside a microwave — the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged, so the casing should only be opened by a qualified engineer. Please do not touch any internal components inside the casing. Microwaves contain high-voltage capacitors that can hold a lethal charge even when unplugged, so opening the case is unsafe for testing. The most common reason for this symptom is simply a setting issue: if it was on Defrost (low power), Grill, or Combination mode, it won't heat food properly. If you were using Full Power in standard microwave mode, then the fault lies within the high-voltage heating circuit (likely the capacitor, diode, or magnetron). To help me guide you safely: did you set it to 'Full Power' or 100% for the cook, and were you using a standard microwave mode (not Defrost, Grill, or Combination)?
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.

It was on full power in normal microwave mode, and I tried a cup of water for a minute and it stayed cold. Same on every power level too. The deep hum is quieter than it used to be and there was a loud buzz just before it stopped heating yesterday.

I must stop you here: do not touch any internal components or attempt to test them yourself. The high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when unplugged and is extremely dangerous for anyone without specialist training and equipment. Please put the casing back together immediately and contact a qualified appliance engineer to replace the faulty part.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
